The transform depends only on query_columns (error_upsampling.py:77-100), so it could be done once at line 227 with no change in behavior. This is duplication only, not a bug.

src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:27 hashes `tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))`, and project_ids is typed list[int] (src/sentry/search/events/types.py:182-184). PYTHONHASHSEED randomization only applies to str/bytes (and datetime), not int. Tuples of ints hash the same way in every process: running `hash(tuple(sorted([5,3,100000000001])))` with PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and PYTHONHASHSEED=2 gives the same value (-4993397539313515218), while hash('a') changes. So the claimed inconsistency across restarts/processes doesn't happen. Only theoretical edge cases remain: mixed Python versions or architectures, and 64-bit collisions.

src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:73 (invalidate_upsampling_cache) builds the key with exactly the same formula as line 27, and hash() of an int tuple is deterministic across processes (checked with different PYTHONHASHSEED values). So invalidation targets the same key that the read path writes. Separately, grep finds no callers of invalidate_upsampling_cache in src/ or tests/, so it is currently dead code. That is a different issue from the one the reviewer raised.
